lines.text: No, this was he, Messala,

lines.speaker: Titinius
lines.text: But Cassius is no more.--O setting Sun,

lines.speaker: Titinius
lines.text: As in thy red rays thou dost sink to night,

lines.speaker: Titinius
lines.text: So in his red blood Cassius' day is set,

lines.speaker: Titinius
lines.text: The sun of Rome is set! Our day is gone;

lines.speaker: Titinius
lines.text: Clouds, dews, and dangers come; our deeds are done!

lines.speaker: Titinius
lines.text: Mistrust of my success hath done this deed.

lines.speaker: Messala
lines.text: Mistrust of good success hath done this deed.

lines.speaker: Messala
lines.text: O hateful Error, Melancholy's child!

lines.speaker: Messala
lines.text: Why dost thou show to the apt thoughts of men

lines.speaker: Messala
lines.text: The things that are not? O Error, soon conceived,

lines.speaker: Messala
lines.text: Thou never comest unto a happy birth,

lines.speaker: Messala
lines.text: But kill'st the mother that engender'd thee!

lines.speaker: Titinius
lines.text: What, Pindarus! where art thou, Pindarus?

lines.speaker: Messala
lines.text: Seek him, Titinius, whilst I go to meet

lines.speaker: Messala
lines.text: The noble Brutus, thrusting this report

lines.speaker: Messala
lines.text: Into his ears: I may say, thrusting it;

lines.speaker: Messala
lines.text: For piercing steel and darts envenomed

lines.speaker: Messala
lines.text: Shall be as welcome to the ears of Brutus

lines.speaker: Messala
lines.text: As tidings of this sight.

lines.speaker: Titinius
lines.text: Hie you, Messala,

lines.speaker: Titinius
lines.text: And I will seek for Pindarus the while.--

lines.speaker: Titinius
lines.text: Why didst thou send me forth, brave Cassius?

lines.speaker: Titinius
lines.text: Did I not meet thy friends? And did not they

lines.speaker: Titinius
lines.text: Put on my brows this wreath of victory,

lines.speaker: Titinius
lines.text: And bid me give it thee? Didst thou not hear their shouts?

lines.speaker: Titinius
lines.text: Alas, thou hast misconstrued every thing!

lines.speaker: Titinius
lines.text: But, hold thee, take this garland on thy brow;

lines.speaker: Titinius
lines.text: Thy Brutus bid me give it thee, and I

lines.speaker: Titinius
lines.text: Will do his bidding.--Brutus, come apace,

lines.speaker: Titinius
lines.text: And see how I regarded Caius Cassius.--

lines.speaker: Titinius
lines.text: By your leave, gods: this is a Roman's part:

lines.speaker: Titinius
lines.text: Come, Cassius' sword, and find Titinius' heart.

stage_directions: Alarum. Re-enter Messala, with Brutus, young Cato, Strato, Volumnius, and Lucilius.

lines.speaker: Marcus Brutus
lines.text: Where, where, Messala, doth his body lie?

lines.speaker: Messala
lines.text: Lo, yonder, and Titinius mourning it.

lines.speaker: Marcus Brutus
lines.text: Titinius' face is upward.

lines.speaker: Young Cato
lines.text: He is slain.

lines.speaker: Marcus Brutus
lines.text: O Julius Caesar, thou art mighty yet!

lines.speaker: Marcus Brutus
lines.text: Thy spirit walks abroad, and turns our swords

lines.speaker: Marcus Brutus
lines.text: In our own proper entrails.

lines.speaker: Young Cato
lines.text: Brave Titinius!

lines.speaker: Young Cato
lines.text: Look whether he have not crown'd dead Cassius!

lines.speaker: Marcus Brutus
lines.text: Are yet two Romans living such as these?--

lines.speaker: Marcus Brutus
lines.text: The last of all the Romans, fare thee well!

lines.speaker: Marcus Brutus
lines.text: It is impossible that ever Rome

lines.speaker: Marcus Brutus
lines.text: Should breed thy fellow.--Friends, I owe more tears

lines.speaker: Marcus Brutus
lines.text: To this dead man than you shall see me pay.--

lines.speaker: Marcus Brutus
lines.text: I shall find time, Cassius, I shall find time.--

lines.speaker: Marcus Brutus
lines.text: Come therefore, and to Thassos send his body:

lines.speaker: Marcus Brutus
lines.text: His funerals shall not be in our camp,

lines.speaker: Marcus Brutus
lines.text: Lest it discomfort us.--Lucilius, come;--

lines.speaker: Marcus Brutus
lines.text: And come, young Cato;--let us to the field.--

lines.speaker: Marcus Brutus
lines.text: Labeo and Flavius, set our battles on:--

lines.speaker: Marcus Brutus
lines.text: 'Tis three o'clock; and Romans, yet ere night

lines.speaker: Marcus Brutus
lines.text: We shall try fortune in a second fight.

stage_directions: Alarum. Enter, fighting, Soldiers of both armies; then Brutus, young Cato, Lucilius, and Others.

lines.speaker: Marcus Brutus
lines.text: Yet, countrymen, O, yet hold up your heads!

lines.speaker: Young Cato
lines.text: What bastard doth not? Who will go with me?

lines.speaker: Young Cato
lines.text: I will proclaim my name about the field:--

lines.speaker: Young Cato
lines.text: I am the son of Marcus Cato, ho!

lines.speaker: Young Cato
lines.text: A foe to tyrants, and my country's friend;

lines.speaker: Young Cato
lines.text: I am the son of Marcus Cato, ho!

lines.speaker: Marcus Brutus
lines.text: And I am Brutus, Marcus Brutus, I;

lines.speaker: Marcus Brutus
lines.text: Brutus, my country's friend; know me for Brutus!

stage_directions: Exit, charging the enemy. Cato is overpowered, and falls.

lines.speaker: Lucilius
lines.text: O young and noble Cato, art thou down?

lines.speaker: Lucilius
lines.text: Why, now thou diest as bravely as Titinius;

lines.speaker: Lucilius
lines.text: And mayst be honour'd, being Cato's son.

lines.speaker: First Soldier
lines.text: Yield, or thou diest.

lines.speaker: Lucilius
lines.text: Only I yield to die:

lines.speaker: Lucilius
lines.text: There is so much that thou wilt kill me straight;

lines.speaker: Lucilius
lines.text: Kill Brutus, and be honour'd in his death.

lines.speaker: First Soldier
lines.text: We must not. A noble prisoner!

lines.speaker: Second Soldier
lines.text: Room, ho! Tell Antony, Brutus is ta'en.

lines.speaker: First Soldier
lines.text: I'll tell the news. Here comes the General.--

lines.speaker: First Soldier
lines.text: Brutus is ta'en, Brutus is ta'en, my lord.

lines.speaker: Mark Antony
lines.text: Where is he?

lines.speaker: Lucilius
lines.text: Safe, Antony; Brutus is safe enough:

lines.speaker: Lucilius
lines.text: I dare assure thee that no enemy

lines.speaker: Lucilius
lines.text: Shall ever take alive the noble Brutus:

lines.speaker: Lucilius
lines.text: The gods defend him from so great a shame!

lines.speaker: Lucilius
lines.text: When you do find him, or alive or dead,

lines.speaker: Lucilius
lines.text: He will be found like Brutus, like himself.

lines.speaker: Mark Antony
lines.text: This is not Brutus, friend; but, I assure you,

lines.speaker: Mark Antony
lines.text: A prize no less in worth. Keep this man safe,

lines.speaker: Mark Antony
lines.text: Give him all kindness; I had rather have

lines.speaker: Mark Antony
lines.text: Such men my friends than enemies. Go on,

lines.speaker: Mark Antony
lines.text: And see whether Brutus be alive or dead;

lines.speaker: Mark Antony
lines.text: And bring us word unto Octavius' tent

lines.speaker: Mark Antony
lines.text: How everything is chanced.

stage_directions: Enter Brutus, Dardanius, Clitus, Strato, and Volumnius.

lines.speaker: Marcus Brutus
lines.text: Come, poor remains of friends, rest on this rock.

lines.speaker: Clitus
lines.text: Statilius show'd the torch-light; but, my lord,

lines.speaker: Clitus
lines.text: He came not back: he is or ta'en or slain.

lines.speaker: Marcus Brutus
lines.text: Sit thee down, Clitus: slaying is the word;

lines.speaker: Marcus Brutus
lines.text: It is a deed in fashion. Hark thee, Clitus.

lines.speaker: Clitus
lines.text: What, I, my lord? No, not for all the world.

lines.speaker: Marcus Brutus
lines.text: Peace then! no words.

lines.speaker: Clitus
lines.text: I'll rather kill myself.

lines.speaker: Marcus Brutus
lines.text: Hark thee, Dardanius.

lines.speaker: Dardanius
lines.text: Shall I do such a deed?

lines.speaker: Clitus
lines.text: O Dardanius!

lines.speaker: Dardanius
lines.text: O Clitus!

lines.speaker: Clitus
lines.text: What ill request did Brutus make to thee?

lines.speaker: Dardanius
lines.text: To kill him, Clitus. Look, he meditates.

lines.speaker: Clitus
lines.text: Now is that noble vessel full of grief,

lines.speaker: Clitus
lines.text: That it runs over even at his eyes.

lines.speaker: Marcus Brutus
lines.text: Come hither, good Volumnius; list a word.

lines.speaker: Volumnius
lines.text: What says my lord?

lines.speaker: Marcus Brutus
lines.text: Why, this, Volumnius:

lines.speaker: Marcus Brutus
lines.text: The ghost of Caesar hath appear'd to me

lines.speaker: Marcus Brutus
lines.text: Two several times by night; at Sardis once,

lines.speaker: Marcus Brutus
lines.text: And this last night here in Philippi fields:

lines.speaker: Marcus Brutus
lines.text: I know my hour is come.

lines.speaker: Volumnius
lines.text: Not so, my lord.

lines.speaker: Marcus Brutus
lines.text: Nay I am sure it is, Volumnius.

lines.speaker: Marcus Brutus
lines.text: Thou seest the world, Volumnius, how it goes;

lines.speaker: Marcus Brutus
lines.text: Our enemies have beat us to the pit:

lines.speaker: Marcus Brutus
lines.text: It is more worthy to leap in ourselves

lines.speaker: Marcus Brutus
lines.text: Than tarry till they push us. Good Volumnius,

lines.speaker: Marcus Brutus
lines.text: Thou know'st that we two went to school together;

lines.speaker: Marcus Brutus
lines.text: Even for that our love of old, I pr'ythee,

lines.speaker: Marcus Brutus
lines.text: Hold thou my sword-hilts, whilst I run on it.

lines.speaker: Volumnius
lines.text: That's not an office for a friend, my lord.

lines.speaker: Clitus
lines.text: Fly, fly, my lord! there is no tarrying here.

lines.speaker: Marcus Brutus
lines.text: Farewell to you;--and you;--and you, Volumnius.--

lines.speaker: Marcus Brutus
lines.text: Strato, thou hast been all this while asleep;

lines.speaker: Marcus Brutus
lines.text: Farewell to thee too, Strato.--Countrymen,

lines.speaker: Marcus Brutus
lines.text: My heart doth joy, that yet in all my life

lines.speaker: Marcus Brutus
lines.text: I found no man but he was true to me.

lines.speaker: Marcus Brutus
lines.text: I shall have glory by this losing day,

lines.speaker: Marcus Brutus
lines.text: More than Octavius and Mark Antony

lines.speaker: Marcus Brutus
lines.text: By this vile conquest shall attain unto.

lines.speaker: Marcus Brutus
lines.text: So, fare you well at once; for Brutus' tongue

lines.speaker: Marcus Brutus
lines.text: Hath almost ended his life's history:

lines.speaker: Marcus Brutus
lines.text: Night hangs upon mine eyes; my bones would rest

lines.speaker: Marcus Brutus
lines.text: That have but labour'd to attain this hour.

lines.speaker: Clitus
lines.text: Fly, my lord, fly!

lines.speaker: Marcus Brutus
lines.text: Hence! I will follow.--

lines.speaker: Marcus Brutus
lines.text: I pr'ythee, Strato, stay thou by thy lord:

lines.speaker: Marcus Brutus
lines.text: Thou art a fellow of a good respect;

lines.speaker: Marcus Brutus
lines.text: Thy life hath had some smack of honor in it:

lines.speaker: Marcus Brutus
lines.text: Hold, then, my sword, and turn away thy face,

lines.speaker: Marcus Brutus
lines.text: While I do run upon it. Wilt thou, Strato?

lines.speaker: Strato
lines.text: Give me your hand first: fare you well, my lord.

lines.speaker: Marcus Brutus
lines.text: Farewell, good Strato.--Caesar, now be still:

lines.speaker: Marcus Brutus
lines.text: I kill'd not thee with half so good a will.

stage_directions: He runs on his sword, and dies.
Alarum. Retreat. Enter Octavius, Antony, Messala, Lucilius, and Army.

lines.speaker: Octavius Caesar
lines.text: What man is that?

lines.speaker: Messala
lines.text: My master's man.--Strato, where is thy master?

lines.speaker: Strato
lines.text: Free from the bondage you are in, Messala:

lines.speaker: Strato
lines.text: The conquerors can but make a fire of him;

lines.speaker: Strato
lines.text: For Brutus only overcame himself,

lines.speaker: Strato
lines.text: And no man else hath honour by his death.

lines.speaker: Lucilius
lines.text: So Brutus should be found.--I thank thee, Brutus,

lines.speaker: Lucilius
lines.text: That thou hast proved Lucilius' saying true.

lines.speaker: Octavius Caesar
lines.text: All that served Brutus, I will entertain them.--

lines.speaker: Octavius Caesar
lines.text: Fellow, wilt thou bestow thy time with me?

lines.speaker: Strato
lines.text: Ay, if Messala will prefer me to you.

lines.speaker: Octavius Caesar
lines.text: Do so, good Messala.

lines.speaker: Messala
lines.text: How died my master, Strato?

lines.speaker: Strato
lines.text: I held the sword, and he did run on it.

lines.speaker: Messala
lines.text: Octavius, then take him to follow thee,

lines.speaker: Messala
lines.text: That did the latest service to my master.

lines.speaker: Mark Antony
lines.text: This was the noblest Roman of them all:

lines.speaker: Mark Antony
lines.text: All the conspirators, save only he,

lines.speaker: Mark Antony
lines.text: Did that they did in envy of great Caesar;

lines.speaker: Mark Antony
lines.text: He only, in a general-honest thought

lines.speaker: Mark Antony
lines.text: And common good to all, made one of them.

lines.speaker: Mark Antony
lines.text: His life was gentle; and the elements

lines.speaker: Mark Antony
lines.text: So mix'd in him that Nature might stand up

lines.speaker: Mark Antony
lines.text: And say to all the world, "This was a man!"

lines.speaker: Octavius Caesar
lines.text: According to his virtue let us use him

lines.speaker: Octavius Caesar
lines.text: With all respect and rites of burial.

lines.speaker: Octavius Caesar
lines.text: Within my tent his bones to-night shall lie,

lines.speaker: Octavius Caesar
lines.text: Most like a soldier, order'd honorably.--

lines.speaker: Octavius Caesar
lines.text: So, call the field to rest; and let's away,

lines.speaker: Octavius Caesar
lines.text: To part the glories of this happy day.

lines.speaker: Octavius Caesar
lines.text: THE END
